ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The diagram shows twenty congruent circles arranged in three rows and enclosed in a rectangle. The circles are tangent to one another and to the sides of the rectangle as shown in the diagram. The ratio of the longer dimension of the rectangle to the shorter dimension can be written as $\frac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{p}-q\right),$ where $p$ and $q$ are positive integers. Find $p+q$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: From the attached figure, it can be seen that there are three rows of congruent circles inside a rectangle whose width is greater than its height. The top row has 7 circles, the bottom row has 7 circles, and the middle row has 6 circles; the middle row is horizontally staggered relative to the upper and lower rows, located between two adjacent circles in the upper row or lower row. The circles are tangent to one another, and the outer circles are tangent to the sides of the rectangle. Reasoning: Let the radius of each circle be r. According to the figure, the 7 circles in the top row are arranged horizontally and tangent to one another, so the centers of the top-row circles can be placed at x = r, 3r, 5r, ..., 13r, and therefore the width of the rectangle is 14r. The centers of the middle-row circles are located between adjacent top-row centers, so the horizontal distance from a tangent top-row circle center is r. The distance between the centers of two tangent circles is 2r, so the vertical distance between the centers of two adjacent upper and lower rows is sqrt((2r)^2 - r^2) = sqrt(3)r. The three rows have two such vertical intervals, from the top row to the middle row and from the middle row to the bottom row, and adding the top radius r and bottom radius r, the height of the rectangle is r + sqrt(3)r + sqrt(3)r + r = 2r + 2sqrt(3)r. Since the width is longer, the ratio of the long side to the short side is 14r / (2r + 2sqrt(3)r) = 7 / (1 + sqrt(3)). Rationalizing gives 7 / (1 + sqrt(3)) = 7(sqrt(3) - 1) / 2 = (1/2)(7sqrt(3) - 7) = (1/2)(sqrt(147) - 7). Therefore p = 147, q = 7, and p + q = 154.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/radius setup. From the image, read that the top and bottom rows each contain 7 circles, the middle row contains 6 circles, and the middle row is horizontally shifted halfway between adjacent circles in the rows above and below. Let the common radius be r. Place the 7 top-row centers at x = r, 3r, 5r, ..., 13r, so the rectangle width is 14r. A middle-row center lies horizontally r away from a tangent top-row center, and the distance between their centers is 2r, so the vertical separation is sqrt((2r)^2 - r^2) = sqrt(3)r. There are two such vertical separations from top row to middle row to bottom row, plus r at the top and r at the bottom, so the height is 2r + 2sqrt(3)r. The longer-to-shorter ratio is 14r / (2r + 2sqrt(3)r) = 7/(1 + sqrt(3)) = (7/2)(sqrt(3) - 1) = (1/2)(sqrt(147) - 7). Thus p = 147, q = 7, and p + q = 154.

method.method_draft: Use the triangular-lattice structure of the packing. From the image, the 20 circles form a hexagonal packing pattern: 7 circles along the top, 6 staggered in the middle, and 7 along the bottom. Connect the centers of mutually tangent circles.
